differences_from_lex: INVOICES_TOKENS/INVOICES_PORT/INVOICES_DB environment variables become --tokens tokA:acme,... (port is the skeleton's --port); no database path.

No SQLite/lex-orm: invoices live in memory in App for the life of the process; no persistence requirement; capacity at least 1000 invoices, 503 when full (reference holds 4096 and a 1 MiB customer pool).
No --host / loopback-only requirement: a cancho listener binds the port on all interfaces.
lex-web/lex-schema/lex-orm replaced by std.http/std.json/std.route; 'every query is parameterized' becomes 'the customer filter is data' (exact byte match, injection strings match nothing).
Grants net,sql,env,fs_write become the cancho authority set (args, heap, clock, net_in, conn_accept, conn_read, conn_write, poll, io_write/err_write) checked by cancho authority.

Brief fixes details Lex left open so the attack can be exact: response shapes (invoice has exactly five members, list is an array in ascending id order, errors are {"error":...}), check order (404/405 route, 401, 413, id 404, body 400), 405 for a known path with another method, ids no leading zero and at most 9 digits, customer length counted in code points after trimming, filter percent-decoding ('+' is a space, >1024 raw bytes or bad encoding is 400, empty filter lists nothing), exactly three members so duplicates are rejected.

Requirement 7 (constant-time token compare) is added explicitly; it is not observable black-box, so it has no attack check (reference implements it with xor/or over the longer length and every entry).
pitfalls: Authorization comparison: a prefix or substring match on the token (found by mutation m5, 11 failing checks).
Counting customer length in bytes instead of code points, or before trimming (m7, m9).
Accepting any JSON number for amount_cents (1.5, 5.0, 1e3) instead of an int.
Accepting extra/duplicate members (mass assignment); the 3-member count rule also rejects duplicates.
Body limit off by one (exactly 4096 allowed, 4097 is 413) and the limit applied after parsing (non-JSON oversize body must be 413).
403 or a different body for a foreign id (existence leak); 401 body must be identical for missing and unknown tokens and not echo the token.
A list response over 64 KiB (1000 invoices is about 80 KB) must still be served whole: the skeleton does it, an application that truncates its own buffer does not.

Dropped/adapted checks: lex 'DELETE -> 404 or 405' is now exactly 405; 'trailing space on token' stays [200,401] because std.http trims header value whitespace; lex checks about SQLite grants and DB file removed; added capacity (1000), leading-zero ids, multibyte customers, JSON escapes, same-tenant tokens, 405s, percent-decoding, check order, boundary 4096/4097, big bodies over the skeleton's 16 KiB buffer.

cancho: a row must be exact (an app_new that does not touch the heap cannot declare [heap]); there is no break/continue; res fields of App are reached through the &!App reference (contents(app.field)), growth by reallocation is therefore not possible, so the reference uses fixed-capacity boxed slices.
